title: Password storage and reset flow audit
when: The user wants to know whether an existing app stores and handles passwords safely: hashing, comparison, reset links, change flows and places where passwords might leak.
prompt:
Goal: Findings covering storage format, verification, reset and change flows and leak points, each with severity and fix.
Steps:
1. Storage: classify as plain text, reversible encryption, fast hash (md5, sha1, sha256, salted or not) or slow KDF (scrypt, argon2, bcrypt, PBKDF2 with high iterations); anything but a salted slow KDF is high.
2. Verification: constant time compare, same reply and timing for unknown user and wrong password, throttling per account and address.
3. Reset: token from crypto.randomBytes(32), stored hashed, single use, valid under 60 minutes, voided by a password change; the link host comes from config, never the Host header.
4. Change and reset end other sessions; a change needs the current password or a fresh login.
5. Leaks: search logs, error reports, analytics calls and request dumps for password fields; forms use type="password" with the right autocomplete.
6. Policy: minimum 8 characters, 64 or more allowed, no composition rules, a blocklist of common passwords.
Quality bar:
- Each finding cites file and line and the exact fix.
- Severity follows the impact of a database leak.
- No real password or hash is copied into the report.
Pitfalls:
- Accepting salted sha256 as good enough.
- Skipping the reset flow, often the weakest part.
- Host header injection in reset emails.
Verify:
- [ ] Storage format is classified.
- [ ] Each reset token rule is checked.
- [ ] Logs were searched for password fields.
- [ ] Each finding has severity and fix.
Output: A password section in SECURITY-AUDIT.md.

examples.input: audita como meu sistema guarda senha e o fluxo de esqueci a senha
examples.output: hash format classified, reset token checklist, Host header issue found, log leak search
